column1: # One verdict per endpoint in testdata/api-surface.json, by hand.
# The snapshot is machine-owned: `make api-diff` refetches it from
# favro.com/developer and nothing else writes it. This file is the other
# half — what this server does about each endpoint — and `gates
# api-coverage` holds the two to each other in both directions, offline,
# Columns, tab-separated: METHOD  PATH  VERDICT  DETAIL
#   implemented  DETAIL names the internal/favroapi methods that issue
#                it. The gate checks each one exists, so the verdict is
#   out          DETAIL is why, in a sentence. A verdict of "not yet" is
#                not a reason; if it is only unbuilt, say so and say
# A PATH ending in * covers every endpoint under that prefix, and a
# METHOD of * covers every verb, so a family decided together is one
# row. The gate still checks each endpoint is matched exactly once, so
# a categorical row that quietly covers nothing fails rather than
# reading like one that covers twenty.

column4: Creates a Favro organization. This server binds one organization at startup (§8) and a token scoped to one tenant has no business minting another; there is no model workflow that ends in a new organization.

Renames the organization and rewrites its membership and roles. Both are tenant administration rather than work inside a tenant, and the blast radius is every user of the org — the one write where a model's mistake cannot be scoped by a widget or a card.

Registers an OUTGOING webhook: Favro posts card events to a URL the caller supplies. This server is a stdio process a host starts and stops, so it can never be that URL, and a tool that points Favro at somebody else's endpoint is a tool for configuring a system this server has no part in. Listing and deleting are implemented because removing what somebody else registered needs no receiver. Revisit if an HTTP transport ever lands.

SCIM user provisioning, both versions, every verb. A different product surface with a different audience — an identity provider syncing directory state on a schedule — and a different auth model from the API token this server holds. Nothing a model doing work inside Favro reaches for, and writing the same sentence twenty-three times would make the file longer without making the decision better.
